newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BID TO HAMPER TML, PEARSON DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BID TO HAMPER TML, PEARSON DEAL.

text.p: Caxton Ltd said on Monday it would seek a court order to prevent the possible sale of a stake in Times Media Ltd's (TML) Financial Mail magazine to UK group Pearson plc following a court judgment.

South Africa's Appeal Court on Friday ruled in favour of Caxton's bid to block Independent Newspapers Holdings Ltd, formerly Argus newspapers, and Omni Media Corporation Ltd , owners of TML, from publishing magazines, suburban newspapers and "free-sheets".
Asked if Caxton would seek an interdict to stop the possible sale, Caxton joint managing director Terrence Moolman said: "Yes, probably."
The judgement follows a battle which started in 1991 between Argus Holdings Ltd -- later renamed Omni Media -- and Caxton when the Argus bought a stake in Caxton.
One of the conditions for the sale was that the Argus, and its units, would undertake not to publish "free sheets", suburban newspapers and magazines.
Moolman said this agreement was never complied with.
"They flagrantly decided in 1991 to ignore the undertaking and attack our business," Moolman said.
While the court case was in progress, Omni Media sold its stake in the Argus to Tony O'Reilly's Independent Newspapers Plc in March 1995 and increased its stake in TML to 91.9 percent.
Moolman said Caxton would launch an interdict against TML, Pearson deal as the Financial Mail magazine would now be part of the agreement that was not adhered to.
"Our gripe is not with TML but the old Argus, now Omni Media. Through Omni Media the Argus owns Times Media," he said.
TML managing director Roy Paulson told Reuters on Monday TML was a separate company at the time of the undertaking between Omni Media and Caxton and was therefore not directly affected by the ruling.
Paulson said that Omni Media would also not force TML to take action detrimental to its shareholders.
He said talks with Pearson were proceeding well and were at a "mature" stage.
Pearson Plc, publisher of the Financial Times, confirmed last month it was negotiating to acquire an interest in TML's Financial Mail and Business Day.
Omni Media management was not immediately available for comment.
